name: Meta Henrico

model_completeness.definition: All eight contribution-account categories contain sourced or labeled modeled values, and GDP, employment, and wage county-comparison modules are populated. Comparison gaps are descriptive and do not establish causal facility effects.

research_value: Documented transition to operation and four later panel years.

history.date_note: This is a stored historical observation. Completion, grand opening, lease and operating-by dates are not automatically commissioning dates. Campus timing does not date every building.

sources.title: IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas, release 2026.02.09

research_updates.title: Identity, opening, and evidence-scope search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: operator facility identity and opening chronology. Query/identifier: Meta/Facebook Henrico Data Center, White Oak, August 5 2020; date range 2017-2026. Documents inspected: Meta opening page, current factsheet, county announcements, and planning records. Result: useful - confirms the campus was serving traffic by August 5, 2020, but public evidence generally covers the multi-building campus rather than the selected inventory footprint.

source.title: Henrico County, We Are Online!
source.notes: Dated operator opening announcement. Completed construction activity and completion-dependent forecasts are separately worded. Operator self-report, not an independent employment or expenditure audit. Solar-project jobs elsewhere in the state are excluded from campus employment.

research_updates.title: Land-use and phased site-plan search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: zoning, plan of development, and land use. Query/identifier: POD2017-00431 Project Echo, parcel 849-704-6939, Technology Boulevard/Portugee Road; date range 2017. Documents inspected: September 14, 2017 Planning Commission agenda and archived minutes. Result: useful - approved a roughly 328-acre, five-building phased program on county water/sewer; no phase-to-inventory-building crosswalk or cost schedule was published.

source.title: Henrico Planning Commission agenda - POD2017-00431 Project Echo
source.notes: The approved plan of development identifies Project Echo on part of parcel 849-704-6939 at Technology Boulevard and Portugee Road. Phase I comprised two connected one-story buildings with mechanical penthouses totaling approximately 1 million square feet; three future buildings totaled 1.5 million square feet on a roughly 328-acre M-2 site served by county water and sewer.

research_updates.title: Original announcement and public-infrastructure context searched
research_updates.notes: Search family: local economic-development announcement and public infrastructure. Query/identifier: Facebook Henrico 970,000 square feet $750 million $40 million White Oak; date range 2017. Result: useful for initial forecast and site history, but the more-than-$40-million county figure covered park-wide infrastructure accumulated before the project and cannot be assigned as Meta public cost.

source.title: Henrico officials join governor to announce plans for Facebook facility
source.notes: The contemporaneous announcement describes a planned $750 million, 970,000-square-foot Facebook data center on approximately 300 acres at White Oak, more than 100 planned full-time jobs, a separate $250 million statewide solar commitment, and more than $40 million of preexisting county investment in park-wide infrastructure. The infrastructure amount is not project-allocable and is not encoded as a public cost.

research_updates.title: Expansion forecast chronology searched
research_updates.notes: Search family: project expansion, capital, construction, and operating forecasts. Query/identifier: Facebook Henrico expansion three 500,000-square-foot buildings $750 million; date range 2018-2020. Result: useful - preserves the $750 million incremental source projection and the planned five-building scale; forecast construction and operating jobs are not reclassified as actuals.

source.title: Henrico officials, governor announce major expansion of Facebook data center
source.notes: The county announced a planned additional $750 million and three 500,000-square-foot buildings, bringing the program to five buildings and more than 2.4 million square feet. It projected approximately 1,500 construction jobs and more than 200 full-time operating jobs after completion; those forecasts are retained separately from later reported actuals.

research_updates.title: Opening, local-partner, and pandemic-support search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: local opening record, contractors/suppliers, and community support. Query/identifier: Facebook Henrico officially online suppliers $830,000; date range 2020. Result: mixed - confirms online status and named support components, but 'numerous local partners and suppliers' has no payment, vendor geography, contract value, or employment amount. Community components overlap the later cumulative total and are not added.

source.title: Facebook's Henrico Data Center is officially online
source.notes: The EDA reports the data center officially online, more than $1 billion invested, 1,500 construction jobs supported, and numerous local partners and suppliers. It also reports nearly $830,000 of pandemic-era support, including $475,000 for small businesses and nonprofits and $280,000 for public-school hotspots and food; the components are not added to the later cumulative operator total.

research_updates.title: Assessor portal and exact parcel/address searches completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: assessor and parcel records. Query/identifier: GPIN 849-701-2260; 6200 Technology Boulevard; 7301 Technology Boulevard; Scout Development LLC; date range current snapshot. Documents inspected: Henrico real-property search interface and county board parcel records. Result: partial - identifiers were corroborated, but no stable text-rendered parcel valuation or personal-property account was captured, so audited principal-taxpayer values are used instead.

source.title: Henrico County real property search
source.notes: The live search interface supports GPIN/PID and street-address queries. Exact identifiers 849-701-2260, 6200 Technology Boulevard, and 7301 Technology Boulevard were cross-checked against county board records, but no stable text-rendered current parcel detail or personal-property account was captured; fiscal values therefore rely on the audited principal-taxpayer table.

research_updates.title: Land, deed, easement, and address continuity searched
research_updates.notes: Search family: land and county-board property records. Query/identifier: Scout Development 6200 Technology Boulevard GPIN 849-701-2260 quitclaim easement; date range 2021-2025. Result: useful for ownership/address continuity only; no deed consideration, assessment, project investment, public expenditure, or selected-building allocation was reported.

source.title: Henrico County Board of Supervisors regular meeting minutes, February 11, 2025
source.notes: A quitclaim and easement item states that Scout Development, LLC owns 6200 Technology Boulevard, GPIN 849-701-2260. The record confirms a current project-linked address and parcel identifier but reports no transfer price, assessment, construction cost, or inventory-building allocation.

research_updates.title: Audited fiscal, taxpayer, incentive-agreement, and bond search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: ACFR, principal taxpayers, incentive agreements, debt, and bonds. Query/identifier: Scout Development LLC, Facebook, 6200/7301 Technology Boulevard; fiscal years 2017-2025. Result: useful - two combined real/personal assessed-value stocks were found. The report discloses agreement mechanics but says grant amounts are confidential, and no project-specific bond proceeds, debt service, taxes paid, or marginal service costs were located.

source.title: Henrico County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2025
source.notes: The principal-taxpayer table identifies Scout Development LLC as the company that bought and developed the site containing the Facebook data center and reports combined real- and personal-property assessed values of $2,045,241,378 for calendar 2024 and $2,364,906,425 for calendar 2025. The notes also describe 2017 and 2022 performance agreements covering facilities at 6200 and 7301 Technology Boulevard and state that grant amounts are confidential under Virginia law.

research_updates.title: State incentive award and compliance search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: state economic-development awards and performance compliance. Query/identifier: Scout Development LLC, Henrico, MOU 9/26/2017, performance date 6/1/2021, DCRSUT; date range 2017-2023. Result: useful - state table verifies the project achieved at least 50 jobs and $150 million capital investment. Actual exemption benefits and amounts above the thresholds were not disclosed.

source.title: VEDP Board of Directors public meeting book - Data Center Retail Sales and Use Tax Exemption performance
source.notes: The DCRSUT project table lists Scout Development LLC in Henrico as a single-user project with a September 26, 2017 MOU and June 1, 2021 performance date. The project is marked post-performance and as having achieved the statutory minimums of 50 new jobs and $150 million of capital investment; the table does not disclose actual tax benefits or amounts above those thresholds.

research_updates.title: Budget, capital-plan, public-cost, and revenue search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: county budgets, capital plans, infrastructure, and service cost. Query/identifier: Facebook revenue, White Oak, Portugee Road pumping station, schools technology; fiscal years 2022-2024. Result: negative for a bounded account - a $2 million Facebook-labelled revenue allocation and system capital projects appear, but payer, tax type, facility scope, causation, and Meta-attributable cost shares are absent.

source.title: Henrico County Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Approved Budget
source.notes: The budget reports a $2 million General Fund Revenue (Facebook) allocation to school technology and lists White Oak-area utility capital projects, including the Portugee Road Water Pumping Station. It does not identify the revenue type, payer account, facility allocation, or any project-attributable share of system capital or annual public-service costs, so no fiscal or public-cost record is created.

research_updates.title: Current operating-employment and community-funding search completed
research_updates.notes: Search families: operator operating headcount, community funding, recipients, and service-cost statements. Query/identifier: Meta Henrico operational jobs supported, schools, nonprofits, grants, sponsorships, and full utility costs; current through September 6, 2026. Result: useful - more than 200 supported jobs and more than $4.2 million cumulative local funding, but no dated employee census, wage or residence data, complete audited award ledger, or utility bill. Recipient grants are overlapping components.

source.title: Meta Henrico Data Center information sheet
source.notes: The current two-page operator factsheet reports more than $1 billion invested, 1,500 peak skilled-trade workers, more than 200 operational jobs supported, more than 200 grants and sponsorships since 2019, more than $4.2 million of direct local funding, and eight Virginia clean-energy projects adding 700 MW. It says Meta pays the full costs of energy and county water and wastewater service but publishes no bills, rates, or project-specific public-cost amounts.

research_updates.title: Recipient-reported county grant search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: county appropriations and recipient grant records. Query/identifier: Meta Data Center Action Grants $35,000 library computer work-and-play stations; fiscal year 2023. Result: useful - exact county-received amount and purpose, retained only as a component of the broader cumulative total.

source.title: Henrico County June 2023 budget amendments
source.notes: The county amendment appropriates $35,000 received through Meta Data Center Action Grants for public-library computer work-and-play stations. This recipient-reported amount is a component of broader Meta community funding and is not additive to the operator's cumulative total.

research_updates.title: Facility electricity, water, and emissions search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: operator environmental data. Query/identifier: Henrico (VA) facility rows, calendar 2020-2024. Result: useful - 2024 electricity 948,859 MWh and water withdrawal 92 megaliters, plus emissions context. Electricity is a direct record; water is retained only as a transparent unit-conversion synthesis because no compatible canonical direct metric exists.

source.title: Meta 2025 Environmental Data Index
source.notes: Facility tables report Forest City electricity consumption of 535,555 MWh, water withdrawal of 16 megaliters, zero market-based Scope 2 emissions and 144,104 metric tons CO2e of location-based Scope 2 emissions for 2024. Values are rounded to whole displayed units and the methodology permits utility, meter, design-estimate or proxy inputs where applicable. Only electricity is normalized as a canonical source record because the shared evidence metric registry lacks compatible annual water-withdrawal and facility-emissions definitions.

research_updates.title: Air-permit inventory and exact permit-ID search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: environmental permits and backup generation. Query/identifier: Scout Development LLC, registration/application 52629-4, Henrico; date range 2019-2026. Result: partial - issued permit and date confirmed, but indexed primary records yielded no generator count, capacity, runtime, fuel consumption, emissions, or operating-cost observation.

source.title: Issued air permits for data centers
source.notes: The issued-permit inventory lists Scout Development LLC, registration/application 52629-4, Henrico County, Piedmont region, Article 6 minor new-source review, issued June 27, 2019. The indexed record does not expose generator count, nameplate capacity, runtime, fuel use, emissions, or cost.

research_updates.title: Utility tariff, regulator, and rate-impact search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: utility commission, special contract, tariff, and load. Query/identifier: Scout Development LLC/Facebook, Dominion Schedule RF, >=30 million kWh incremental load; date range 2017-2026. Result: partial - regulator confirms the arrangement and threshold but publishes no Henrico-specific usage, demand, bill, interconnection cost, payment, or customer-rate impact.

source.title: Virginia State Corporation Commission 2019 Annual Report
source.notes: The report says approved Dominion Schedule RF arrangements support Scout Development LLC/Facebook and apply to customers with at least 30 million kWh of incremental annual load. It describes renewable-energy-certificate purchases but discloses no Henrico-specific usage, demand, bill, rate impact, interconnection cost, or customer payment.

research_updates.title: Municipal water, wastewater, billing, and capacity search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: water utility, rates, customer billing, capacity, and discharge. Query/identifier: Scout/Facebook/Meta, 6200 and 7301 Technology Boulevard; date range 2017-2026. Result: negative for monetary and meter details - general schedules exist, while customer bills, metered volumes, capacity reservations, connection charges, marginal cost, and discharge remain unpublished.

source.title: Henrico County water and sewer rates
source.publisher: Henrico County Department of Public Utilities
source.notes: The current rate page and linked utility materials were searched for Scout, Facebook, Meta, 6200 Technology Boulevard, and 7301 Technology Boulevard. They publish general schedules but no customer-level meter volumes, bills, capacity reservations, connection charges, marginal service cost, or discharge amount.

research_updates.title: Contractor, construction-value, supplier, and workforce-residence search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: contractor and supplier contribution. Query/identifier: DPR Meta Henrico five buildings, local vendors, subcontractors, payroll, workforce residence; date range 2017-2026. Result: identity and scale only. No contract value, project spending, vendor payments, supplier location, payroll, worker-hours, or residence share supports a supplier or household model.

source.title: Meta Henrico Data Center
source.notes: The contractor profile identifies DPR's role and describes the Henrico program as a five-building, roughly 2.4-to-2.5-million-square-foot campus begun in October 2017. It publishes no contract value, annual spend, vendor payments, payroll, worker residence, supplier geography, or inventory-building allocation.

research_updates.title: Court, judgment, and lien search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: Virginia court records. Query/identifier: Scout Development LLC, Facebook, Meta, Henrico, 6200/7301 Technology Boulevard; date range 2017-2026. Result: no authoritative project-specific judgment, damages award, lien amount, or enforceable public cost was located; absence from indexed results is not proof of no litigation.

source.title: Virginia Circuit Court case information
source.notes: Party-name searches for Scout Development LLC, Facebook, and Meta combined with Henrico and the 6200/7301 Technology Boulevard identifiers did not produce an authoritative project-specific judgment, damages award, lien amount, or enforceable cost suitable for the account. The negative result does not prove that no litigation exists.

research_updates.title: County GDP source and comparison-input search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: federal county GDP. Query/identifier: BEA real GDP, Henrico County FIPS 51087, years 2012-2024. Result: useful only as governed county-panel input; the aggregate cannot identify Meta or support causal attribution.

source.title: BEA API for Data Retrieval User Guide
source.notes: The guide documents county GDP and income tables used by the governed 2001-2024 county panel. County aggregates do not identify Meta, isolate the campus, or establish a causal project effect.

research_updates.title: County employment and wage comparison-input search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: federal QCEW employment and wages. Query/identifier: Henrico County FIPS 51087, years 2012-2024. Result: useful only as governed county-panel input; suppression and aggregation prevent a Meta establishment payroll or headcount and do not identify causal project effects.

source.title: QCEW Searchable Databases
source.notes: The portal provides county employment and wage histories used by the governed comparison panel. Published county-industry aggregates do not disclose a Meta establishment payroll or support causal attribution to the Forest City campus.

research_updates.title: County establishments, payroll, and supplier-proxy search completed
research_updates.notes: Search family: federal County Business Patterns. Query/identifier: Henrico County FIPS 51087, data-processing and construction industries, 2017-2024. Result: negative for project-specific contribution - confidentiality and county aggregation prevent Meta payroll, supplier payments, vendor geography, or household spending observations.

source.title: County Business Patterns Data
source.notes: County Business Patterns provides county-industry establishments, employment and payroll. Employer confidentiality and county aggregation prevent a project-specific Meta payroll, supplier-spend, or operating-headcount observation.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net.
legacy_first_entry_note: Meta establishes that its mapped Henrico Data Center began serving traffic on August 5, 2020. Henrico County's seven current source records do not establish a complete history or exclude earlier carrier, state-government, banking, utility, university, or enterprise data centers in greater Richmond.
scope_note: Provisional private-sector research candidate. Owner/operator history, project boundaries and lifecycle require review. Membership does not verify current operation or establish economic impact.
project_description: Meta's Henrico Data Center is a hyperscale campus operated by Meta in White Oak Technology Park, Henrico County, Virginia; the inventory project represents one mapped building footprint, while public project evidence generally covers the campus. Henrico approved Project Echo in September 2017 as a phased 328-acre development with two connected Phase I buildings of about 1 million square feet and three future buildings totaling 1.5 million square feet, and construction began in October 2017. Meta reported the campus serving traffic on August 5, 2020; later county records distinguish 6200 Technology Boulevard from facilities at 7301 Technology Boulevard, so campus and later-building facts are not allocated to the selected footprint.
